tomas: quick sanity check — ran long-ctx bench (32k/64k) across H100, A100, MI300 for Llama-70b / Mistral-8x / Qwen-72b. seeing weird kernel mismatch on MI300 for rope vs gqa fallback. anyone else?

sophia: saw that earlier. MI300 falls back to generic attention path for rope-gqa when sequence > 48k, huge latency jump. is this from our kernel selector? :thinking_face:

alex: yes selector picks mi-optimized kernel only for seq <= 48k for now. fallback path uses slower matmul+custom-rope patch. latency numbers?

maria: pasted quick numbers from the run (bs=1, tok/s measured at steady state):
```
Model    GPU    ctx   kernel    p50(ms)  p95(ms)  tok/s
Qwen72  H100   32k   rope-gqa   320      520      370
Qwen72  MI300  32k   rope-gqa   410      910      280
Qwen72  MI300  64k   rope-gqa   1250    2300      90
Mistral  H100  64k   gqa        480     840      260
Llama70 H100  64k   gqa        560     980      210
```

jiwoo: ouch MI300 64k looks terrible. when MI300 falls back is it due to kernel memory layout (blocked matmul) or a constraint in the ROCm kernel?

alex: it's a mix. fallback triggers when we can't fit fused KV+rope kernel workspace within per-block alloc heuristics. For MI300 we have a smaller per-SM temp budget compared to H100 for some kernels.

bench-bot: profile gist -> https://internal.redwood/dashboard/bench/1957654321/compare (contains traces + flamegraphs) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

tomas: thanks — can we try two things: 1) run with prefix/KV cache enabled to see delta (to isolate per-token compute vs prefix recompute), 2) run quant4a and q5_kv on MI300 to see memory/throughput tradeoff?

maria: running now — commands: 
```
# run baseline
runtest --model qwen-72b --kernel rope-gqa --gpu mi300 --region eu-west1 --bs 1 --seq 65536 --cache disabled
# run with cache
runtest --model qwen-72b --kernel rope-gqa --gpu mi300 --region eu-west1 --bs 1 --seq 65536 --cache enabled
# run quant profile
runtest --model qwen-72b --kernel rope-gqa --gpu mi300 --quant q4a --kv_quant q5_kv --bs 1 --seq 65536
```

sophia: FYI we also saw improved p95 when we force kernel to 'gqa-fallback' on H100 for certain seq lengths — the cheaper H100 fused kernel wins until 48k then it flips. might be worth extending the H100 threshold too.

alex: agree. but need to be careful: H100 fusion uses a custom blocksize that assumes float16 alignment; quant paths on H100 are separate. if we extend threshold, add a guard to validate workspace alloc at kernel init.

jiwoo: quick numbers from cache-enabled run (maria posted full logs):
```
Qwen72 MI300 64k cache=on -> p50 430ms p95 760ms tok/s 240 (vs 1250/2300 before)
Mistral MI300 64k cache=on -> p50 380ms p95 690ms tok/s 270
```

maria: quant run results (approx):
```
Qwen72 MI300 q4a+q5_kv 64k -> p50 290ms p95 520ms tok/s 360 (memory down ~40%)
Qwen72 H100 64k q4a+q5_kv  -> p50 210ms p95 380ms tok/s 520
```

tomas: great — so caching buys us a lot, quant helps even more. For capacity sizing: if product needs steady 200 qps at 64k with Qwen72 and 95th p95 target <700ms, how many MI300s? using measured tok/s ~360 translate to qps?

alex: rough calc: 1 request ~ 64k tokens? depends. assuming avg 512 output tokens per request => per-GPU throughput ~360 tok/s -> ~0.7 req/s (360/512). so need ~ 200 / 0.7 ~= 285 GPUs. with batching and concurrency you'd drop that by ~2x. so estimate ~140 MI300s reserved. big number.

jiwoo: alternative: route heavy longctx to H100 pool (higher tok/s) and keep MI300 for mid/short. mixed routing policy can reduce committed MI300 by ~60% in sim.

sophia: kernel work: propose a short patch to kernel selector heuristics: check workspace_estimate <= gpu_temp_budget && prefer fused-kernel-if-quant-available. I'll open PR with toggles per-region (eu vs us perf diffs noted).

maria: PR would help. Also let's add a perf test to our CI that exercises 32k/64k paths on MI300 specifically (so we catch regressions).

tomas: agree. next steps: alex to own kernel selector change, sophia to add perf CI, jiwoo to draft routing policy simulation for longctx. I'll file infra tickets and tag infra-bot.

infra-bot: ticket created -> INFRA-1127 (mi300 longctx perf CI) ; ticket created -> PERF-2046 (kernel-selector heuristics) ; assigned: alex, sophia, jiwoo

alex: I'll start a small bisect to see if a recent ROCm runtime bump changed workspace behavior. assigning myself.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll upload full benchmark CSV + traces to the bench gist and add a short note on recommended capacity split (H100 for long-tail, MI300 for bulk).

tomas: perfect. tagging @sophia @alex @jiwoo — sync in 1h to review PRs and CI design. :thumbsup:
